meta.title: Shopify: Five Times the Business, the Same Stock
meta.dek: Revenue is nearly five times what it was in February 2021 and the stock is back at that week's price. The agents have arrived and every one of them checks out with Shop Pay. What does $153 assume, and who gets paid when an agent does the buying?
meta.price_note: Nov 4, 2026 close, 4:00 PM EST; the overnight session showed $151.19
meta.type: Commerce platform: merchant software plus payments

verdict.sentence: Shopify grew 32% again and every new shopping agent checks out with Shop Pay, but at $153.03 the stock sits at its February 2021 price on a still-rich multiple, and the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle: Watch.
verdict.breaks_if: Agents become a toll: Shopify discloses a fee or revenue share paid to an agent operator, or merchant-solutions gross margin falls below 37% for two quarters while management points to wallet or agent economics. Then the agent channel stops being new volume at today's take rate and becomes old volume at a lower one.
verdict.price_implies: between the Base and the Bull (owner EPS ≈[[Priced-in.owner_eps]] in 2031 for 9%/yr)

call: The operating case got stronger again. Q3 revenue grew 32% against a low-thirties guide, GMV grew 30% in constant currency for the sixth straight quarter, and in the US Shopify's merchants are now taking nearly half of all incremental e-commerce. The agent question moved too. Muse, Instinct, Claude Duet and Grok Bot all launched with Shop Pay as the wallet, Shop Pay GMV grew 50%, and the president says agent orders carry the same merchant fees as the online store. What the market has right is the price of all this. At $153.03 the enterprise value is about 64 times this year's free cash flow and about 80 times owner earnings after stock pay. Per-share owner earnings can compound at [[compounding]] a year in my Base and the stock still earns [[pw_return]], because the multiple has to come down by more than half. Spot already sits between my Base and my Bull. What the market may have too little of is the economics question. Analysts asked three times on the call who gets paid when an agent completes the purchase, and the answer covered only the case where the agent sends the shopper to the merchant's own site. The Base and Bull exits assume growth well above GDP after 2031, which I accept because the Base is still growing close to 20% a year then. The verb is not probability-fragile. Even with no Bear at all, the Base and Bull mix does not reach 13%.

tests.claim: That growth holds above 25% as comparisons harden.
tests.test: Q4 2026 revenue growth of at least 28% against the low-thirties guide, and a Q1 2027 revenue guide at a mid-twenties rate or better, both in the Q4 release (about mid-February 2027). Q3 delivered +32% on top of +32% a year earlier.
tests.if_fail: 15 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **Watch / Hold**, entry ≤[[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That agents stay a channel, not a toll.
tests.test: Through the Q2 2027 results (early August 2027): no disclosed fee or revenue share paid by Shopify to an agent operator on Shop Pay checkouts, and merchant-solutions gross margin of at least 37% in every quarter (38.5% in Q3 2026, 36.8% in the mix-heavy Q4 2025, so Q4 2026 is compared with that). An agent default that routes a named partner's checkouts away from Shop Pay also fails.
tests.if_fail: 15 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **Watch / Hold**, entry ≤[[test2.entry]].

tests.test: FY2026 gross-profit growth of at least 25% and a free-cash-flow margin of at least 18% in the 10-K (February 2027). Nine months stand at +30% and 18.5%.
tests.if_fail: 10 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **Watch / Hold**, entry ≤[[test3.entry]].

return_math.compounding: Base owner earnings per share grow from ≈$1.64 in FY2026 to [[Base.owner_eps]] in FY2031, [[Base.cagr]] a year, with no dividend: that is the compounding rate at a flat multiple. Re-rating takes about 23 points a year off the Base return, because the exit at 35× is well under half of today's ≈90× FY2026 owner earnings. All of the gap to the hurdle is the multiple.
return_math.price_implied: At 9%, spot needs owner earnings of [[Priced-in.owner_eps]] a share in FY2031 at 35×: revenue of about $44B and an operating margin near 22%, between my Base and Bull. On free cash flow alone, EV of ≈$186B on ≈$2.9B prices about 18% growth for ten years at 9%, then 4%.
return_math.epv: Owner earnings power today is ≈$2.1–2.3B. Capitalized at 9% that is ≈$24B, or about $19 a share, plus ≈$8 of cash and stakes: ≈$27 against $153. About 82% of the price pays for growth. The Bear's ≈[[Bear.value]] is about three times EPV, so even the Bear assumes the business keeps growing.
return_math.base_rate: Revenue of ≈$15B sits in the $12–25B bucket. The Base's ≈22% nominal growth (about 19–20% real) over five years is reached by roughly 3–4% of such companies, and the Bull's ≈25% by under 3% ([`compounding.md`](../../frameworks/compounding.md)). Shopify has been in that tail for a decade, which is why the Base is Probable rather than Plausible; the Bull is Plausible and the Bear Probable.
return_math.terminal_growth: Implied perpetual growth on owner earnings at 9%: Bull [[Bull.g]], Base [[Base.g]], Bear [[Bear.g]]. The Bull and Base exceed the 4.95% Treasury, so their exit multiples assume Shopify is still growing well above GDP after 2031. I accept that for the Base because the business is still growing close to 20% in FY2031, but it is a real assumption.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing in the low-to-mid teens at year ten on e-commerce share of retail, offline, B2B and international, with operating margin still rising, so the business compounds past the horizon; the 35× exit assumes exactly that.
return_math.rr_note: The downside is a toll on the agent channel plus a normal growth company's multiple, not a broken business.
